intelligence.title: A Number in a Box Is Not a Report

intelligence.essence: A stat shown as a lone number in a black box is plumbing wearing a label. Data becomes a report when it has shape (a chart), direction (a trend), and meaning (a sentence a human can feel). NayaNET should be known for the most alive data presentation anywhere — living intelligence you can see breathing, not digits sitting in boxes.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn opened the flagship Reports and found three black boxes: a 3 that said WALL POSTS, and two cousins like it. Everything underneath was real — live counts from the page's own tables — and none of it was alive. His question is the standard now: "Is that the most beautiful graphs and stats page you could ever make?" If the honest answer is no, the page is not done, no matter how correct the plumbing is.
intelligence.simple_view: Showing someone the number 3 is like telling them "you have three friends" and walking away. Showing them a glowing ring that fills up, bars that grow day by day, and a sentence that says "your wall is waking up" — that's telling the story of the number.
intelligence.grandma_view: A number alone doesn't tell you if things are getting better or worse, or whether to smile about it. A good report is like a good neighbor: it shows you the picture, tells you which way things are heading, and says it in plain words.
intelligence.naya_view: The flagship pages already carried the living machinery — animated bars, a donut that fills, glow pulses, fade-up entrances — in a dormant CSS layer, while the Reports block used none of it. The failure class is the same one composition cured at page level, one level down: presence of parts is not experience of parts. Verification must now score each block as an experience: function, feeling, position, space, intuition — and for data, shape + direction + meaning.
intelligence.ai_view: Correctness is the floor, not the finish. The gap between "the data is real" and "the page is alive" is exactly the gap between an 8.5 engine and a 6.5 experience — and users only ever meet the experience.

machine_view.title: A Number in a Box Is Not a Report
machine_view.machine_section: RULE: a metric surface is DONE only if it renders (a) magnitude, (b) at least one of {composition, trend, comparison}, and (c) a generated human sentence interpreting it. Verification: served-bytes check for chart elements bound to live values + a human-eye pass. A bare count node (number + label) FAILS the reports predicate regardless of data correctness.
